slots.label: Heading 1
slots.default: Switching IT support provider: what actually happens

slots.label: Paragraph 1
slots.default: The most common reason London businesses stay with a provider they have outgrown is the fear that changing will be disruptive. In practice, moving managed IT support is an onboarding exercise rather than a migration, and most of it happens in the background.

slots.label: Paragraph 2
slots.default: Look at what notice your existing agreement requires before you commit to anything. This is the one item that genuinely dictates timing, and it is worth knowing before conversations start.

slots.label: Heading 3
slots.default: Gather what already belongs to you

slots.label: Paragraph 3
slots.default: Make sure you can obtain your own documentation, licence records and administrator credentials. These belong to you rather than to your outgoing provider, and having them to hand makes the handover straightforward.

slots.label: Heading 4
slots.default: Onboarding, with your team still working

slots.label: Paragraph 4
slots.default: We review your systems, set up the tooling we need for remote assistance and monitoring, and start supporting your team. Nothing needs to be rebuilt, and your staff keep working as normal while it happens.
